claim: The topological entanglement entropy (TEE) signature in a Rydberg blockade chain, accessible via the Rydberg tweezer correlated ansatz (PAPER-2026-060), constitutes a measurable bulk-boundary entanglement structure that is formally equivalent to the MERA entanglement structure underlying our holographic force law (alpha~4), implying that the same QuEra Aquila hardware run designed for HYP-2026-017 can simultaneously measure TEE and the holographic force exponent alpha, providing a joint test of two distinct predictions of the AdS/CFT correspondence on a single neutral-atom platform.
confidence_rationale: Low confidence because the formal equivalence between TEE in a quantum spin liquid phase (PAPER-2026-060) and the MERA entanglement structure in our holographic force measurement (SIM-2026-015) has not been demonstrated analytically. PAPER-2026-060 uses a correlated time-dependent ansatz to access topological phases, while our MERA uses a fixed variational circuit. The PXP Hamiltonian (PAPER-2026-061) realizes an Ising CFT, not a topological phase, so the TEE claim applies to a different parameter regime. Low confidence reflects the speculative cross-domain leap; however, the experimental proposal is straightforward and would generate useful data regardless of whether the formal equivalence holds.
test_design: 1. Design a unified Rydberg circuit that (a) prepares the blockade-MERA state for holographic force measurement (per HYP-2026-017 protocol) and (b) allows measurement of topological entanglement entropy via the Kitaev-Preskill or Levin-Wen protocol (tripartite CMI on boundary spins). 2. Run on QuEra Aquila (cloud, AWS Braket). For a 16-atom chain, measure: (a) CMI(A:C|B) at separation dr=1..6 for holographic force law (HYP-2026-017 measurement), (b) Tripartite CMI on boundary partition (A, B, C, D regions) for TEE = S_A + S_B + S_C - S_AB - S_BC - S_AC + S_ABC. 3. Test whether the Rydberg blockade chain is in a topological phase (TEE > 0) or a trivial Ising CFT phase (TEE = 0) at the operating point. 4. Compare: does the holographic force power-law alpha differ between the topological and trivial phases? If TEE > 0 correlates with alpha deviating from 4.0, there is a potential link between topological order and holographic force law.
refutation_criteria: Hypothesis is refuted if: (a) TEE = 0 at the Rydberg PXP operating point (i.e., the system is in the Ising CFT phase, not a topological phase) — this would confirm the PAPER-2026-060 and PAPER-2026-061 results are from different parameter regimes and cannot be measured simultaneously, OR (b) the holographic force power-law alpha is identical within error bars in the topological and trivial phases, establishing that TEE and alpha are independent observables with no formal connection. A null result on the joint measurement is scientifically meaningful and publishable.
hardware_required: QuEra Aquila (256 neutral-atom tweezer, cloud via AWS Braket). Same hardware run as HYP-2026-017 — no additional hardware required. Additional classical analysis: Python/NumPy entropy computation from measurement outcomes. Estimated cost: marginal addition to HYP-2026-017 budget (~$200-500 extra shots for TEE measurement settings).

feasibility_notes.hardware: Identical to HYP-2026-017: QuEra Aquila cloud via AWS Braket. Marginal additional shots for TEE measurement: ~10,000-20,000 shots for tripartite entropy estimation across 3 boundary partitions. Additional cost: ~$200-500. No new hardware required.
feasibility_notes.circuit: TEE measurement (Kitaev-Preskill protocol) on 16-qubit chain: requires measuring S_A, S_B, S_C, S_AB, S_BC, S_AC, S_ABC for boundary partitions. Each entropy estimated via shadow tomography or direct measurement of Renyi-2 entropy. This is within QuEra Aquila's demonstrated capabilities for medium-scale entanglement characterization. No additional gate depth — measurement settings are different, not deeper circuits.
feasibility_notes.math: Kitaev-Preskill TEE protocol is mathematically sound. The speculative element — whether TEE and MERA holographic entanglement are formally equivalent — has no known proof or refutation. This makes it a genuine open question, not an unfalsifiable speculation. If TEE = 0 at the PXP operating point, hypothesis is cleanly refuted. If TEE > 0 and correlates with alpha~4, it opens a new research direction. Both outcomes are publishable.
feasibility_notes.resource: Marginal cost only: ~$200-500 additional cloud shots on the same QuEra run as HYP-2026-017. Classical post-processing adds ~2 hours of NumPy entropy computation. Net additional investment is negligible.

pipeline_provenance.conjecture_stage: Generated from the intersection of PAPER-2026-060 (TEE via Rydberg blockade correlated ansatz) and PAPER-2026-061 (PXP MERA = Ising CFT holographic forces) with our existing MERA holographic force measurement (SIM-2026-015). The key insight is that QuEra Aquila runs are expensive but the marginal cost of measuring TEE alongside alpha~4 on the same shots is near-zero. Even if the formal equivalence claim is wrong, the experiment provides two simultaneous measurements on the same Rydberg platform, doubling the scientific output per dollar. The speculative core — TEE ~ holographic entanglement = force law entanglement — is a genuine open question in the AdS/CFT literature and would be a meaningful finding either way.
